children: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot.

The lawsuit said that The L Suite trained its chatbot Lloyd on copyrighted works including at least one ACC report, and that it "brazenly" promoted Lloyd with an image of the report and an ACC trademark.
Spokespeople for ACC and The L Suite did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the complaint.

The Washington-based ACC has more than 48,000 members and publishes content, including continuing legal education materials, surveys and white papers. The L Suite, which calls itself "the leading general counsel community on its website," announced the launch of its Lloyd chatbot in May.
The L Suite said in a press release that Lloyd "combines foundational AI capabilities with the trusted judgment of thousands of accomplished in-house legal executives."
The ACC said in its complaint that an L Suite video promoting Lloyd displayed the cover of an ACC report.
"As a result, there can be no doubt that The L Suite was specifically aware that its Lloyd platform was utilizing ACC materials," the lawsuit said.

The ACC also alleged that The L Suite violated its trademark rights in the phrase "By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" by using "Built By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" in its Lloyd advertising.
The ACC requested monetary damages and a court order blocking The L Suite from using its trademarks and copyrighted materials.
The case is Association of Corporate Counsel v. The L Suite Inc, U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01138.
For the ACC: Robert Leighton and Paul Sauerteig of Goldberg Kohn
For The L Suite: attorney information not yet available
